scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Liquidity runway = liquid reserve ÷ monthly obligations (spending + interest).
scenes.vo: Banks fail from liquidity (can't pay today) more often than from solvency (owe more than they own). Track both. First, Assets: everything you own, at market value: collateral, yield positions, reserves. Next, Liabilities: everything you owe: loans, margin, any payables. Then, Equity equals assets minus liabilities. This is what's actually yours. Also, L.T.V. = debt divided by collateral. Your bank's leverage. And finally, Liquidity runway equals liquid reserve divided by monthly obligations (spending + interest).

scenes.title: Worked example: $300,000 collateral, $60,000 debt at 5%, $40,000…
steps: Obligations $5,250/month ($250 of it interest) → reserve covers 7.6 months
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. $300,000 collateral, $60,000 debt at 5%, $40,000 stablecoin reserve, $5,000 a month spending: the calculator Equity $280,000 times L.T.V. 20% , health factor 4.0. Obligations $5,250 a month ($250 of it interest) to reserve covers 7.6 months. Policy checks: L.T.V. at most 30% ✓ , health factor at least 2 ✓ , reserve at least 6 months ✓.

scenes.q: Why track liquidity separately from equity?
scenes.a: You can be solvent and still be forced to sell at the worst time if you can't meet obligations today.
